source: WHO, Heat and health fact sheet
text: During a heatwave stay out of the sun between 11am and 3pm, keep the home cool, drink water regularly even if not thirsty, and avoid alcohol and heavy meals. Check on elderly people, young children and people with chronic illness at least once a day.

source: WHO Europe, Heat-health action plans guidance
text: Infants and young children, people over 65, outdoor workers and people with heart, lung or kidney disease are at highest risk of heat illness. Warning signs of heat exhaustion include heavy sweating, dizziness, headache, nausea and muscle cramps.

During heatwave alerts in Pakistan schools should avoid outdoor assemblies and sports in the afternoon, children should carry water bottles, wear light coloured loose cotton clothes and cover the head when walking home.

Heatstroke is a medical emergency: body temperature above 40 C, hot dry skin, confusion or fainting. Move the person to shade, cool them with wet cloths and fanning, give water if conscious, and call 1122 immediately.

source: US NWS, Heat index chart and risk levels
text: Heat index 27-32 C caution, fatigue possible with prolonged exposure. 32-41 C extreme caution, heat cramps and exhaustion possible. 41-54 C danger, heat exhaustion likely and heatstroke possible with prolonged activity. Above 54 C extreme danger.

source: OSHA, Heat illness prevention for outdoor workers
text: Outdoor labourers should follow water, rest, shade: drink a cup of water every 15 to 20 minutes, take rest breaks in shade, schedule heavy work for early morning, and new workers need several days to acclimatise.

AQI 0-50 good. 51-100 moderate, unusually sensitive people should reduce prolonged exertion. 101-150 unhealthy for sensitive groups such as children, older adults and people with asthma or heart disease. 151-200 unhealthy for everyone. 201-300 very unhealthy. Above 300 hazardous.

WHO guideline levels: PM2.5 annual mean 5 micrograms per cubic metre and 24-hour mean 15. PM10 annual mean 15 and 24-hour mean 45. Long exposure above these levels raises risk of heart and lung disease.

source: US EPA AirNow, Asthma and air quality
text: People with asthma should keep quick-relief inhalers with them, avoid outdoor exercise when particle pollution is unhealthy for sensitive groups or worse, and exercise indoors or when air quality is better, often early morning.

source: US EPA, Particle pollution and exercise
text: When PM2.5 is high choose easier activities such as walking instead of jogging, shorten outdoor time, and stay away from busy roads and industrial areas where particle levels are highest.

source: WHO, Ambient air pollution fact sheet
text: Children breathe more air per kg of body weight and are more vulnerable to air pollution. On high pollution days keep windows closed during peak traffic hours and limit children's outdoor play near roads.

source: PMD Karachi, Sea breeze and coastal weather notes
text: In Karachi the sea breeze usually lowers coastal temperatures in the evening, but when the sea breeze is suspended during a heatwave evenings stay hot and humid. Check humidity and wind before evening walks or jogs on the beach.
